citations.paraphrase: By contrast, this fatwa rules glycerine from an animal source not permissible (fat generally from a non-halal animal) and advises checking the source before use — representing the cautious side of a genuine scholarly disagreement over unverified-source glycerine.

citations.paraphrase: Where haram content (pig-derived or improperly-slaughtered animal glycerine) is certain or strongly suspected, it is obligatory to avoid eating, drinking or using it; only a lawfully-slaughtered source (or genuine istihalah) makes it permissible — supporting strict avoidance of doubtful-source E422.

citations.paraphrase: A Hanafi fatwa holding that where the source of glycerine is uncertain and cannot reasonably be confirmed, it is permissible to assume it is halal, since investigating every ingredient's source causes undue hardship — the permissive stance a lenient consumer relies upon (given regarding externally-used products).

citations.paraphrase: For non-meat products the basic presumption is permissibility unless haram content is established from trustworthy sources, and glycerine whose animal fat has undergone istihalah (chemical transformation into a genuinely different substance) can become permissible — but pig-derived or improperly-slaughtered glycerine remains haram, so the presumption is not unconditional.
citations.sourceName: Islam Q&A — Fatwa 97541 (citing the Standing Committee for Issuing Fatwas)

citations.paraphrase: Plant and synthetic glycerine is permissible, but glycerine obtained from an animal source is not permissible since the fat is generally derived from a non-halal animal; one should check the source of the glycerine before use and exercise caution when it is unverified.
